name: afk-compact
description: Smart auto-compaction for long unattended Claude Code sessions: compacts at a clean turn boundary, saves the summary as a handoff, and keeps the work going.

handoff_root.title: Handoff folder [default ~/.local/state/afk-compact/handoffs]
handoff_root.description: Where the plugin keeps your handoffs (notes a fresh session can pick the work up from) and its saved copy of every compaction summary, in one subfolder per repository and ticket or topic. Default ~/.local/state/afk-compact/handoffs ($XDG_STATE_HOME/afk-compact/handoffs when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute path), outside ~/.claude, where Claude Code asks before every write in the default permission mode; while this is unset (or set to that default), handoffs an earlier version saved in ~/.claude/handoffs are still read, never written. Change it to keep them somewhere else, such as a synced drive, but keep it outside any git repository.

log_dir.title: Log folder [default: empty = inside the handoff folder]
log_dir.description: Where the plugin keeps its local logs (which hold no conversation text) and its per-compaction records. Empty (the default) means the .watch folder inside the handoff folder; set a path only if you want the logs kept apart from the handoffs.

disposable_root.title: Temporary evidence folder [default ~/.local/state/afk-compact/disposable]
disposable_root.description: Where the plugin copies temporary files the session referred to (for example test output or logs in a temp folder), in one dated folder per day, so they are still there after the system clears its temp folder. Default ~/.local/state/afk-compact/disposable ($XDG_STATE_HOME/afk-compact/disposable when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute path), outside ~/.claude, for the same reason as the handoff folder; while this is unset (or set to that default), copies an earlier version made in ~/.claude/trash-staging are still read, never written. Nothing in it is deleted automatically; /afk-compact:prune lists old folders and deletes them after your yes.

disposable_keep_days.title: Evidence keep days (age for prune) [default 0]
disposable_keep_days.description: How many days you plan to keep the temporary evidence copies: the handoff reports print it, and /afk-compact:prune lists evidence older than it (14 days while it is 0). The plugin never deletes on its own. Default 0 means "kept until you remove them".

evidence_quota_mb.title: Evidence size warning (MB) [default 500]
evidence_quota_mb.description: Size, in MB, at which the plugin warns that the saved evidence and summary copies of one ticket or topic folder have grown large. Default 500 MB; it only warns and never deletes, so raise it if the warning is noise, lower it to hear sooner, or set 0 for no warning.

queue_cmd.title: Question queue program [default: empty = off]
queue_cmd.description: Optional: the path of a program of your own that collects the questions an unattended session needs to ask you, so they wait in one queue as well as in the handoff (the program must follow the contract in assets/queue-contract.md in the plugin folder; the README's "Connect your own question queue" shows a minimal one and how to test it). Empty (the default) turns this off and the plugin calls nothing; only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored.

triggers.title: Plugin compactions
triggers.description: Lets the plugin start compactions itself at a clean point, nudge the model toward one, and tell the session to carry on afterwards. Default true; set false if you only want every compaction written as a handoff, saved and checked, while Claude Code alone decides when to compact.

compact_target_tokens.title: Compaction target (tokens) [default 400,000]
compact_target_tokens.description: Conversation size, in tokens, at which the plugin compacts (has Claude Code summarize the conversation and continue from the summary) as soon as the model finishes a turn, instead of waiting for Claude Code to compact in the middle of a task. Default 400,000 (minimum 100,000); lower it to compact earlier and more often, raise it to keep more history in view; on smaller context windows the plugin lowers it by itself.

compact_soft_max_tokens.title: Mid-turn nudge point (tokens) [default 600,000]
compact_soft_max_tokens.description: Conversation size, in tokens, at which the plugin asks the model, once, in the middle of a long turn to reach a stopping point so the compaction can run cleanly. Default 600,000 (minimum 150,000); keep it above the compaction target, and lower it if long turns keep running into Claude Code's own mid-task compaction.

native_window_tokens.title: Claude Code compaction window (tokens) [default 0 = the window Claude Code reports]
native_window_tokens.description: The context size within which Claude Code runs its own automatic compaction; the plugin keeps its own thresholds below Claude Code's compaction point (about 33,000 tokens under this window). Default 0 means the compaction window Claude Code reports (set by CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, your autoCompactWindow setting or the model's default), with its own compaction point when it reports one; a Claude Code that reports none: the window your autoCompactWindow setting names, else the model's context window. Enter a number only if Claude Code compacts within another window (values under 100,000 count as 100,000).

boundary_delay_ms.title: Wait before acting (ms) [default 2,000]
boundary_delay_ms.description: How long, in milliseconds, the plugin waits after a turn ends before it compacts or sends a turn of its own; a message you send during the wait cancels it. Default 2,000 (2 seconds; 500 ms after a nudged turn); raise it if you want more time to step in before the plugin acts.

cooldown_ms.title: Minimum gap between compactions (ms) [default 30,000]
cooldown_ms.description: Shortest time, in milliseconds, between two compactions the plugin starts, so a session that fills up fast cannot compact over and over. Default 30,000 (30 seconds); raise it if you see plugin compactions bunched together.

max_auto_continues_per_hour.title: Automatic continues per hour [default 6]
max_auto_continues_per_hour.description: How many times in any one hour the plugin may tell a session to keep working by itself after a compaction. Default 6 (allowed 0 to 10); lower it to limit unattended usage, or set 0 so that every run stops after its compaction and waits for you (by default the model is first given a turn to write a handoff, see Handoff before stopping).

handoff_turn.title: Handoff before stopping [default true]
handoff_turn.description: true (the default): when the plugin will not continue the work by itself after the coming compaction, it first gives the model one extra turn to write a handoff you can resume from later; false skips that turn, which saves its usage but leaves only the compaction summary.

handoff_turn_max_tokens.title: Handoff turn budget (tokens) [default 64,000]
handoff_turn_max_tokens.description: How many tokens the extra handoff-writing turn may use; the plugin keeps that much room free below Claude Code's own compaction point. Default 64,000 (allowed 20,000 to 150,000); raise it if handoffs get cut short, lower it on small context windows, where a large budget makes the plugin compact earlier.

precompact_turn.title: Handoff before each planned compaction [default true]
precompact_turn.description: true (the default): before each compaction the plugin starts at the compaction target, the model gets one extra turn to write a handoff while it still sees the whole conversation; false: the plugin records its own checkpoint without that turn, which uses less of your usage allowance.

measured_block.title: Measured facts for the summarizer
measured_block.description: When on, the plugin adds freshly measured facts (git branch, commit, changed files, background jobs) to the instructions Claude Code's summarizer gets; this applies only when the plugin's main module shapes the compaction. Default false, because the first turn after every compaction gets these facts, measured again, anyway; turn it on if summaries keep getting them wrong.

auto_evidence.title: Copy cited temp files
auto_evidence.description: After each compaction, copy temporary files the session mentioned (such as logs or test output in a temp folder) into the temporary evidence folder, with size limits and a secret check, so they are still there when the work resumes. Default true; set false if you do not want these copies on disk.

warn_ui.title: Pop-up warnings and compaction line
warn_ui.description: Show the plugin's short pop-up notices in Claude Code when something needs your attention, for example when it pauses automatic work or saves a handoff, and one dim line in the conversation after each compaction saying whether it went well (the model does not see it). Default true; set false for fewer interruptions and check /afk-compact:status instead.

watcher.title: Local compaction logs [default true]
watcher.description: true (the default) keeps local logs of how each compaction went, without any conversation text, and nothing is ever sent (you can share them yourself with /afk-compact:report); false stops new log entries and keeps the ones already written.

stall_min.title: Stalled job alert (minutes) [default 60]
stall_min.description: How long, in minutes, a background job must have been running before the local logs may flag it as stalled in /afk-compact:status; it is flagged once it has run this long and its output file has not changed for the last 15 minutes; a job whose output cannot be checked is never flagged. Default 60; lower it to hear about stuck jobs sooner, raise it if your jobs normally run for a long time with quiet stretches.

cache_ttl_s.title: Prompt cache lifetime (seconds) [default 300]
cache_ttl_s.description: How long, in seconds, the local logs assume Claude Code's prompt cache (the stored conversation that makes the next request cheaper) stays fresh; a large compaction after a longer pause is flagged as likely costly. Default 300 (5 minutes); set 3600 if your sessions use the one-hour cache, so pauses that cost nothing are not flagged.

deny_class_patterns.title: Blocked-tool categories [default: empty = the built-in rules]
deny_class_patterns.description: Your own rules for sorting blocked tool calls (permission denials) into categories in the local logs, written as category=pattern pairs (pattern: a regular expression) separated by ';', where the category is sleep-poll, routing, secret, write-guard, scope or other. Empty (the default) uses the built-in rules; change it only if your own hooks block tools with messages the built-in rules put in the wrong category.

repo_roots.title: Repositories that may receive handoffs [default: empty = no repository]
repo_roots.description: Main checkout folders, separated by ';', into which each published handoff may also be exported so a team can review and commit it; a repository also has to opt in with a .claude/handoffs.json file. Empty (the default) keeps handoffs only in your private handoff folder; only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored.

relaunch_auto.title: Restart lost background jobs [default on]
relaunch_auto.description: on (the default): when a resumed session finds that a background job (such as a long test run) was lost when Claude Code exited, it starts the job again by itself if the job is read-only or on your allowlist and every safety check passes, otherwise it asks; shadow only logs what it would have done and asks; off always asks (only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored).

relaunch_allow.title: Commands allowed to restart by themselves [default: empty = none]
relaunch_allow.description: Patterns (regular expressions, each starting with ^), separated by ';', for commands that are safe to run twice, such as a local test or build, which a resumed session may then restart by itself after a lost-job check. Empty (the default) means only read-only jobs restart by themselves; a command chained with others, one that reaches outside your machine, or a production command always asks (only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored).

relaunch_quiet_s.title: Lost job quiet time (seconds) [default 120]
relaunch_quiet_s.description: When the plugin cannot tell when a lost background job ended, the job's output must have been silent for this many seconds before the job counts as stopped and may be restarted. Default 120 (allowed 30 to 3,600); raise it for jobs that normally go quiet for longer.

unattended_prod_reads.title: Unattended production checks [default false]
unattended_prod_reads.description: false (the default): a resumed session asks before any command that touches production and offers it for you to run, unless an approval you gave names that read-only command; true: a read-only production check the session writes itself may run without asking. Changes to production always ask, and so do production commands copied from a handoff unless an approval you gave names that read command (only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored).

prod_patterns.title: Extra production patterns [default: empty = the built-in rule only]
prod_patterns.description: Extra patterns (regular expressions), separated by ';', that mark a command as touching production, on top of the built-in rule, which looks for prod, production or prd as a separate word or part (as in --context=prod-eu). Empty (the default) means the built-in rule only; add your own environment or host names so the plugin asks before those commands too (these patterns can only make it ask more).

idle_handoff_turn.title: Idle handoff turn [default true]
idle_handoff_turn.description: true (the default): if a long session sits idle and nobody will compact it before Claude Code's one-hour prompt cache (the stored conversation that keeps the next request cheap) expires, the plugin gives the model one turn, about 49 to 56 minutes in, to write a handoff (the idle handoff turn, which does not compact); false never runs that turn, which saves its usage (it costs several times as much as an idle compaction).

idle_compact.title: Plugin idle compaction [default true]
idle_compact.description: true (the default) turns on plugin idle compaction: when a conversation at the idle-compaction minimum or more (200,000 tokens by default) has been idle for about 54 to 56 minutes and native idle compaction (Claude Code's own) has not run, the plugin compacts it itself before the one-hour prompt cache expires, so coming back costs less (terminal sessions only, for now); false: the plugin never compacts idle sessions, and the idle handoff turn runs instead where it applies.

idle_handoff_min_tokens.title: Idle handoff turn: minimum size (tokens), not for compaction [default 200,000]
idle_handoff_min_tokens.description: The smallest conversation, in tokens, that gets the idle handoff turn; it is not an idle-compaction threshold, except when keep-warm stops with a job still open (see keep_warm_hours). That turn writes a handoff without compacting and runs only from this value up to the idle-compaction minimum (CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS, 200,000 by default), since native or plugin idle compaction takes the sessions above it; when the plugin does not compact (idle_compact false, for example), it runs above it too. Default 200,000 (allowed 100,000 to 1,000,000), the same as that minimum, so by default no session gets the turn while the plugin compacts; lower it to cover medium-size sessions too. A work lane that reads finished after an idle compaction (until your next message) gets the turn at any known size.

idle_handoff_near_limit.title: Idle handoff turn: near a usage limit [default run]
idle_handoff_near_limit.description: run (the default): the idle handoff turn runs even when one of your usage limits (the five-hour or seven-day plan window, or a spend limit) is at 90% or more, so you get the handoff anyway; it then counts toward a nearly used allowance, and with extra usage on for your plan, usage past the limit may be billed. skip-spend: no such turn while a spend limit (a money cap, for example a Claude gateway's) is at 90% or more; it still runs near a plan limit. skip: no such turn near any limit. Plugin idle compaction and keep-warm do not go by this value: they follow their own limit rule (README: Near a usage limit).

idle_digest.title: Away summary after an idle compaction [default off]
idle_digest.description: off (the default in this version): when a session compacted while you were away has finished its work or is only waiting on you, the plugin sends no turn of its own and asks for no summary; the next reply starts nothing new and says in one line where the work stands, then what needs you. submit: with nothing still running, the plugin sends one turn right away that prints a short summary (what is done, what is left, what needs you), ready when you return; return sends nothing and puts that summary at the top of the reply to your next message, which saves the turn.

keep_warm_hours.title: Keep the cache warm while background jobs run (hours) [default 6]
keep_warm_hours.description: How many hours the plugin keeps an idle session's one-hour prompt cache (the stored conversation that keeps the next request cheap) warm while one of that session's own background jobs (an agent, a workflow or a background shell; a teammate only while it works, not while it waits idle for a message) is still running: about every 50 minutes it sends one small hidden request that reads the cache and adds nothing to the conversation, so the turn the job's result opens does not read the whole conversation again at full price. When that time is up and a job is still running, the plugin compacts the session while the cache is still warm, from idle_handoff_min_tokens up (the idle handoff turn runs there instead only with idle_compact false or automatic compaction off). It never runs while you are simply away with nothing running, nor with the five-minute cache, and stops near a usage limit (README: Near a usage limit) or when a turn starts. Default 6 (allowed 0 to 24); 0 turns it off, which saves those requests (each one counts toward your usage limits as a cached read of the conversation).

ticket_pattern.title: Ticket id pattern [default [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+]
ticket_pattern.description: A regular expression that finds a ticket id (such as ABC-123) in the git branch name, so that handoffs for one ticket share one folder; if the pattern has a group in parentheses, that group is the id. Default [A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+ (ids like ABC-123); change it to match your tracker's ids (an invalid pattern falls back to the default, and folders made earlier are still found).

secret_extra_rules.title: Extra secret rules [default: empty = the built-in rules only]
secret_extra_rules.description: Your own rules for spotting secrets in handoffs and copied files, added to the built-in ones and separated by ';': HARD:pattern blocks the handoff and withholds the file, WARN:pattern warns and masks the match (for HARD and WARN the pattern is a regular expression), and NAME:wildcard withholds files whose names match a simple wildcard such as *.pem (not a regular expression). Empty (the default) means the built-in rules only; add rules for your own token formats, they can only withhold more (only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored).

resume_proceed.title: Manual resume continues after its report [default true]
resume_proceed.description: true (the default): when you run /afk-compact:resume yourself, it reports what it found and then carries on with the next step; false: it stops after the report and waits for your go-ahead. Resumes after the plugin's own compactions are not affected, and when your settings file, a flag and an environment variable disagree, false wins.

handoff_reuse_window_min.title: Reuse a recent handoff (minutes) [default 15]
handoff_reuse_window_min.description: When the model starts a handoff on its own less than this many minutes after the last one, and nothing has changed since (same commit, same files, no new decisions), the plugin reuses that handoff instead of writing a new one. Default 15 (allowed 0 to 60); 0 turns this time-based reuse off (a handoff is still reused when nothing at all happened since the last one), a higher value saves usage when handoffs come often.

evidence_total_max_mb.title: Evidence copy limit (MB) [default 50]
evidence_total_max_mb.description: The most data, in MB, that one evidence copy run (after a compaction, or for one handoff) copies in full; files beyond it are listed as withheld and left where they are, and nothing is deleted. Default 50 (allowed 10 to 500); raise it if large logs you need later are being withheld, lower it to save disk space.

watch_quota_mb.title: Log size warning (MB) [default 50]
watch_quota_mb.description: When the plugin's local logs grow past this size, in MB, it shows a storage warning; nothing is deleted. Default 50 (allowed 0 to 10,000); 0 turns the warning off, raise it if you keep large logs on purpose.

protected_branches.title: Extra protected branches [default: empty = the built-in list only]
protected_branches.description: Branch names or wildcard patterns, separated by ';', that count as protected on top of the built-in list (the remote's default branch, main, master, develop, staging, release and hotfix branches and similar): a push to one, or a merge into one, always asks you again, whatever you approved before. Empty (the default) means the built-in list only; add your own deployment branches, for example qa-env;uat/*, and note that entries can only add, never unprotect a built-in branch (only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored).

restart_on_update.title: Restart on Claude Code update (beta) [default off]
restart_on_update.description: on: right after a compaction, with nothing running and nobody typing, the plugin restarts the session on a newly installed Claude Code and keeps the same conversation (not active in this version yet, see /afk-compact:status); shadow only logs what it would do; off (the default) never restarts (only your settings file counts for this option, flags and environment variables are ignored).

driver_skills.title: Loop skills to resume [default: empty = the built-in list only]
driver_skills.description: Names of extra skills, separated by ';', that drive a session as a repeating work loop, like the built-in gsd-autonomous, gsd-execute-phase, gsd-manager, superpowers:executing-plans and superpowers:subagent-driven-development; when such a loop is clearly still running at a compaction, the plugin starts it again afterwards so the loop goes on. Empty (the default) means the built-in list only; add your own loop skills (a paused, finished or unclear loop is shown to the model but never restarted, and a skill the session never used is never run).
